author: Tripo AI (Tripo3D) model generated by the game owner; prepared for the remake by Stjörnufar
license: Tripo3D output generated on the owner's paid Tripo plan, used under Tripo terms
rightsNote: The owner generated this model on a paid Tripo plan (see dist/assets/dinosaurs/TRIPO-NOTE.txt). Keep a copy of the Tripo terms in force at publication.
decisions: The owner chose teal for her, with the coral sail of the owner's own concept (2026-10-16; STYLE.md section 3), and real sizes: Uggeðla is 14 m nose to tail, 7.3 m to the top of her sail. Like every character but Grameðla she has no teeth. The wade is for a later chapter, where she keeps station by the water.
modifications: Unrigged Tripo export in 8 parts (386,258 triangles, three 2048 px textures: base colour, metal/roughness, normal map; one double-sided material), standing on two feet in mid-stride (her right foot 1.4 m ahead) with her neck and head turned 16 degrees to her left, facing -X. Welded across UV seams and the seams between parts (192 edges split at T-junctions, 52 pinholes filled, 12,273 seam vertices welded), decimated as one mesh with the head keeping 1.6 times the share of the rest (5,129 of 37,500 triangles), and split back into its 8 parts, closed (remake/tools/blender-decimate.py, Blender 5.2; kept as source/spinosaurus-parts.glb, which the command reproduces byte for byte). The sail is a closed shell 15 to 40 cm thick (at 14 m) welded to the body and the tail's root, not a thin sheet, so it stays in the one closed skin and the single-sided material shows it from both sides; its scalloped top edge came through the decimation within 1.3 cm of the source's on average. Baked by remake/tools/bake/bake-tailed-biped.js (run with bake-character.mjs): turned to face +X (yaw 180), scaled to 14 m long (7.27 m to the top of the sail), stood on the ground with the origin between the feet, soles flattened onto the ground; the parts told apart by position and seams (tail, body with the neck, sail, two whole legs hip to toes, head with both jaws, two whole arms shoulder to claws); the neck and head turned back 15.8 degrees to face forward about the vertical where the head's own axis crosses her midline (1.85 m in front of the hips), the turn fading out over 1.3 m down the neck and the arms turning with their seams, then the whole scaled back to 14 m (x0.990); rigged with 24 bones; smooth skin weights agreeing across the seams, the head part riding its bone whole; five clips authored in code (tailed-biped-clips.js); one skinned mesh with one matte single-sided material (roughness 0.62, no metalness, normal map at 0.8), base colour (no recolour) and normal map as 1024 px JPEG, the metal/roughness map dropped. Then the face pass and the mouth pass (below).
rig: Our bake tool for tailed bipeds (Grameðla's), taught legs and arms of one part, a stance in mid-stride, a sail and a head turned aside. Bones: root, Hips, Spine, Chest, Neck, Head, Tail1-Tail6, Left/Right Thigh, Shin, Foot (digitigrade: the Foot, at the raised heel, carries the metatarsus, toes and claws as one, as the engine's footing plants a biped's), Left/Right UpperArm, LowerArm, Hand, and the Jaw from the mouth pass under the Head; identity rest rotations. Tripo stood her in mid-stride, so each leg keeps its own knee, heel and toes as the model has them (only the hips are mirrored); the knee is where the leg's centre line, going up from the heel, stops leaning forward. An arm of one part gets its elbow and wrist where its centre line (the middles of bands of equal distance over its surface from the shoulder's seam) bends most. The Head joint is at the top of her neck, the middle of the head's seam with the body (neck=0.7: the Neck joint 0.7 m further down the neck), and the head part rides the Head bone whole, so her long crocodile snout never bends; the jaw the mouth pass cut rides the Jaw. The sail follows the back below it: the spine chain's weights where it stands along her (the tail's first bones, Hips, Spine and Chest; its front, over the root of the neck, takes the Chest's), never the neck. Clips: idle 4.0 s (breathing, a slow look about, the tail swaying; the feet planted); walk 2.8 s, 3.2 m a cycle (1.14 m/s; a foot lands flat and sweeps back at exactly that speed, its heel peels up about the toes as the other foot lands), the legs posed by the engine's two-bone IK (engine/ik.js); kink 2.4 s (a friendly nod: the chin lifts, the head dips twice, the second time less, the tail wags; the feet planted); happy 2.4 s (two bobs on bent knees, the head up and rocking, the little arms paddling, the tail swishing; the feet planted); wade 4.2 s, 2.18 m a cycle (0.52 m/s): slow steps through shallow water, the hips 0.19 m lower than at rest and the body leaning 10 degrees forward, the neck bent 42 degrees down at its root and the head turned 26 degrees back up so the tip of her snout hangs 1.8 to 2.0 m above the ground, low over the water, the feet lifted high out of it, each on the ground for 70 % of the cycle, and the tail sweeping wide from side to side for balance, a wave down its length. With a sail the clips bend the back a third as much as Grameðla's, so the sail never stretches or folds: its top edge keeps its length within 1 % in every clip and its skin's edges within 3 %. Every clip loops. In a scene the engine's footing plants her feet in walks, starts, stops and turns on the spot; walkTo(points, { clip: 'wade' }) wades her, the actor measuring the wade's own speed.
pose: Rest pose on two legs, the small arms held up in front, long crocodile snout, tall sail along the back, tail straight out behind; faces -X; 0.98 units long, 0.51 high to the top of the sail.
sourceTextures: three 2048 px JPEG: base colour, metal/roughness, normal map; one double-sided material
facePass: Eyes found in the colour map by remake/tools/bake/face.js (eyes.js) and written into the GLB as extras on the skinned mesh (face.eyes: per eye its centre, frame, outline and lid and lash colours, in bind space), for the eyelids the engine builds in code (engine/eyelids.js). Her amber eyes are 1.18 m apart and 5.8 m up.
mouthPass: A jaw cut by remake/tools/bake/mouth.js: her head part holds both jaws, so the pass splits the triangles along the groove between her upper and lower jaw (the line given in the head frame, read off gridded side views of both sides and the groove's notch measured slice by slice, from behind the corner of her smile to the tip of her snout at f = 1.95) in front of f = 0.3, gives the jaw side its own vertices there (69 triangles split, 73 lip vertices opened; snap=0.003), adds a Jaw bone under the Head at the hinge, blends the jaw in from the hinge to the cut, fills the mouth with a pocket (palate and tongue painted into a free corner of the colour map; 1,680 triangles) and writes face.mouth.talk = 6 (degrees the jaw opens at the loudest syllable: a little, as Grameðla's does when she talks). No teeth. corners=1 (new): a triangle goes to the side its corners off the line are on, so the long thin triangles along her snout's mouth line do not stretch across the open mouth; channel=1 runs the pocket along her long snout under the lips, and fold=0.04,0.01 (new) keeps its fold higher and further back, inside her rounded snout tip with the mouth shut. Cut further back (from f = 0.05) the stretched cheek turned three triangles over at the corners of the mouth, showing a hole and a sliver of the pocket when she talked. Re-exported with GLTFExporter (textures 1024 JPEG), node names kept.
passes: decimateCommand, then bakeCommand, then faceCommand, then mouthCommand (the mouth pass takes its head frame from the eyes the face pass found). Rebaking from the parts reproduces the GLB byte for byte (md5 0683942b4fed4e361c8a0b3b3e3f9842; the parts file's md5 is 2626203b76237b7004c1e734a2a7b592). Grameðla, Þórseðla, Flugeðla and Slóeðla rebake byte for byte with the tools as changed for her.
lookCheck: qa/remake/shots/uggedla-look/ (sheet: the six views; face; rig; the weights of legs, arms, neck, head and sail; the mouth open 6 and 15 degrees; the clips idle, walk, kink, happy and wade, and the wade close up) and qa/remake/shots/spino-look/ (the source as received).
notes: Teal body, deepest along the back and tail, lighter teal flanks, pale mint belly and throat, a coral sail with peach stripes, amber eyes, beige claws and a closed-mouth smile with no teeth showing, as in the concept; STYLE.md section 3 takes Uggeðla's row from this model. Real adult size: 14 m from nose to tail tip, so about 7.3 m to the top of her sail. Look check: qa/remake/shots/spino-look/ (the source) and qa/remake/shots/uggedla-look/ (the bake).
